question: How is H-Net's hierarchy built from dynamic chunking, and did adding a second stage help?
final_text: I couldn't find this in the passages I retrieved from the three papers, so I won't guess. I searched: HNET §3.1 Language Modeling; HNET §3.3 Ablation Studies; HNET §1 Introduction; HNET §3 Experiments.
drafts: H‑Net builds its hierarchy by applying a dynamic‑chunking layer that uses a routing module to draw content‑dependent chunk boundaries and a downsampler that keeps vectors at those boundary positions, thereby creating a compressed representation that can be further processed in subsequent stages [HNET:1:c012][HNET:T6:r03]. The architecture can be iterated, so that the output of one dynamic‑chunking stage becomes the input to a second, yielding a nested, multi‑stage hierarchy [HNET:3.1:c049]. Empirically, adding the second stage improves performance: H‑Net (2‑stage) is significantly better than H‑Net (1‑stage) [HNET:3.1:c049].

H‑Net’s hierarchy is created by a dynamic‑chunking layer that includes a routing module for drawing chunk boundaries and a downsampler that retains vectors at those boundary indicators, reducing sequence length while preserving semantically important positions [HNET:1:c012]. The model can apply this dynamic chunking iteratively, forming two nested stages (S=2) as shown in the architectural overview [HNET:1:c012]. H‑Net (2‑stage) is significantly better than H‑Net (1‑stage), demonstrating that adding a second dynamic‑chunking stage improves performance [HNET:3.1:c049].
